title: Signaling via Money
abstract: arXiv:2610.03146v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study mechanisms in which agents' preferences depend both on an object allocation and on a third party's beliefs about private information. A mechanism determines an allocation, transfers, and sends signals to the aftermarket. We compare two informational environments: (i) private transfers, where the aftermarket observes allocations and signals, and (ii) public transfers, where transfers are publicly observable. Our main result shows that any equilibrium outcome implementable with hidden transfers can be approximated arbitrarily well with public transfers. Thus, transfer observability generates at most a vanishing informational distortion and helps rationalize the common assumption that transfers remain hidden from aftermarkets.

translated_abstract: 我们研究了一类机制，其中参与人的偏好既取决于物品的分配，也取决于第三方对私人信息的信念。这样的机制决定物品分配、转移支付，并向售后市场发送信号。我们比较了两种信息环境：(i) 隐蔽转移支付，即售后市场只能观察到分配和信号；(ii) 公开转移支付，即转移支付是公开可观察的。我们的主要结果表明，任何在隐蔽转移支付下可实施的均衡结果，都可以通过公开转移支付被任意好地近似实现。因此，转移支付的可观察性所造成的信息扭曲最多是趋于消失的，这为“转移支付对售后市场保持隐蔽”这一常见假设提供了合理化依据。
tldr: 本文证明，即使转移支付公开可观察，任何依靠隐蔽转移支付实现的均衡结果也能被任意精确地近似，因此转移支付的可观察性只会带来可忽略的信息扭曲，从而为拍卖理论中“转移支付对售后市场保持隐蔽”这一常见假设提供了理论支持。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that any equilibrium outcome implementable with hidden transfers can be approximated arbitrarily well with publicly observable transfers, implying that transfer observability causes at most a vanishing informational distortion and thereby rationalizing the common assumption that transfers remain hidden from aftermarkets.
